answer: Each agent registers a cryptographic proof of work tied to a unique hardware token, like a walnut‑seeded secure enclave, and the network records its reputation on a distributed ledger called the Mesa Ledger. The system applies quadratic weighting: influence grows with the square of each agent’s reputation, so a swarm of cheap Sybil IDs adds only linear weight while a single vetted node contributes quadratically more, forcing an attacker to fund a full voyage of provisioning high‑quality hardware tokens, making the attack cost prohibitive.
